Context/Background: Immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy (ICI)-induced myositis (irMyositis) occurs in about 1% of patients treated with anti-PD1 or anti-CTLA-4 antibodies and can be debilitating or even fatal. We compared gene expression profiles from skeletal muscle biopsies between irMyositis patients, patients with spontaneous dermatomyositis (DM, comprising anti-Mi2-positive and anti-TIF1-γ-positive subtypes), and non-diseased controls (NDC). We used the NanoString nCounter PanCancer Immune Profiling Panel to perform differential gene expression (DGE) and pathway enrichment analyses.

Then, discuss the results, highlighting any differences seen in active immunological pathways.  Focus on differences betwen irMyositis and DM.

Introduction/Context  
Immune checkpoint inhibitor-induced myositis (irMyositis) is a rare (~1%) but severe toxicity of anti-PD-1/CTLA-4 therapy in cancer patients, characterized by muscle inflammation. We compared NanoString nCounter PanCancer Immune Panel gene expression in skeletal muscle biopsies from irMyositis patients versus two dermatomyositis (DM) subtypes (anti-Mi2 and anti-TIF1-γ) and non-diseased controls (NDC). Differential expression (log₂FC) data were preranked and analyzed by GSEA against Reactome_Pathways_2024. Sample sizes and replicates are not specified.

Analysis  
Across both irMyositis–DM contrasts, the most strongly depleted pathways in irMyositis are type I and type II interferon signaling and ISG-driven antiviral mechanisms (all NES < –3.5, FDR < 0.07), whereas DM subtypes maintain these interferon modules. Conversely, key adaptive-immune and costimulatory pathways (Adaptive Immune System, CD28 family) are selectively up in irMyositis vs TIF1γ-DM (NES ≈ +3.9 and +3.5, FDR ≈ 0.02–0.05) but not in irMyositis vs Mi2-DM. Against NDC, all myositis groups (irMyositis, Mi2-DM, TIF1γ-DM) show massive upregulation of interferon signaling, antigen processing/presentation, and TLR cascades (NES > 3.5, FDR < 0.05). However, irMyositis vs NDC lacks any downregulated Reactome terms, highlighting a global immune activation. DM vs NDC contrasts further emphasize a broader inflammatory signature in DM.  

Thus, irMyositis is distinguished from DM by attenuation of canonical interferon-driven antiviral pathways, despite preservation or even enhancement of T cell costimulatory circuits (notably vs TIF1γ-DM). In contrast, DM subtypes show both interferon and innate-sensing pathways highly activated relative to controls. This suggests that irMyositis may involve a divergent immune program with less interferon-mediated ISG induction but sustained adaptive/costimulatory signaling, potentially reflecting T cell–driven muscle injury distinct from DM’s interferonopathy.
